OVERVIEW TILE METRICS
DETAILED VIEW METRICS
ERG WORKOUT
What each metric means.
Distance
Total distance travelled (GPS), in km or mi based on units setting.
Duration
Total elapsed time of the session.
Pace / Speed
Boat speed, shown in your selected unit (pace per 500m/1km/mile, or km/h/mph). GPS-derived — only valid for comparing the same stretch, direction and tide.
Rate
Average stroke rate, in strokes per minute (SPM).
DPS
Distance per stroke — average boat travel per stroke cycle.
Vel Efficiency
Hydrodynamic efficiency of the boat's speed profile within one stroke. Drag power rises with the cube of speed, so speed swings waste energy versus a constant speed. 100% = perfectly steady hull; typical sculling 93–97%. Higher is better.
Recovery Loss
Speed lost to deceleration during recovery, normalised per second of recovery so values are comparable across stroke rates. Accelerometer-derived, condition-independent. Lower is better.
Drive Accel
Peak forward acceleration during the drive, catch to finish. IMU-derived, in m/s².
Recovery Accel
Peak forward acceleration during the recovery, taken after the small drag-dip that follows the finish. IMU-derived, in m/s².
Impulse
Total positive acceleration during the drive, integrated as a change in velocity (Δv). Higher means more drive power applied to the hull — not a peak value.
Negative Catch Slope
Steepest rate of acceleration FALL going into the catch, as the blade enters and the hull checks. The companion to Positive Catch Slope. Higher means a more abrupt check. Accelerometer-derived jerk, in m/s3.
Catch Accel
Peak negative (backward) acceleration at the catch - the depth of the check. Read off the same stroke curve the graph plots, in m/s2. Closer to zero means a lighter check. Not comparable across boat classes.
Positive Catch Slope
Rate of acceleration rise out of the catch as the drive load comes on. Higher means a sharper, more aggressive catch. Accelerometer-derived jerk, in m/s3.
Ratio
Recovery time ÷ drive time. Higher means a longer, more relaxed recovery relative to the drive.
Stroke Char
Where the peak drive acceleration falls within the drive, as %: 0% = the moment the boat starts accelerating after the catch, 100% = blade exit. The peak time is interpolated between sensor samples and smoothed over 5 strokes. Under 40% = front-loaded, 40–60% = mid-drive, over 60% = back-loaded. Neither is inherently better — it's a technique style that varies by boat type and rower.
Catch Dur
Time from the point deceleration at the catch reaches 30% of its peak depth, until acceleration crosses back through zero. Measures the width of the check, not time-to-peak-force. Accelerometer-derived. Not comparable across boat classes — hull inertia differs, same as Catch Slope.
Drive Time
Time from peak drive acceleration to blade exit — the back half of the drive. Accelerometer-derived, so it covers every stroke regardless of GPS. Catch Dur and Drive Time overlap around the peak, so the true total drive time is less than their sum but more than Drive Time alone.
Avg HR
Average heart rate during the session, in beats per minute.
